source_text:
Εὐφράνθητι, στείρα ἦ οὐ τίκτουσα, ῥῆξον καὶ βόησον, ἡ οὐκ ὠδίνουσα, ὅτι πολλὰ τὰ τέκνα τῆς ἐρήμου μᾶλλον ἢ τῆς ἐχούσης τὸν ἄνδρα. ὃ εἶπεν: Εὐφράνθητι, στεῖρα ἡ οὐ τίκτουσα, ἡμᾶς εἶπεν: στεῖρα γὰρ ἦν ἡ ἐκκλησία ἡμῶν πρὸ τοῦ δοθῆναι αὐτῇ τέκνα.
ὃ δὲ εἶπεν: Βόησον, ἡ οὐκ ὠδίνουσα, τοῦτο λέγει: τὰς προσευχὰς ἡμῶν ἁπλῶς ἀναφέρειν πρὸς τὸν θεόν. μὴ ὡς αἱ ὠδίνουσαι ἐγκακῶμεν,
δ δὲ εἶπεν: Ὅτι πολλὰ τὰ τέκνα τῆς ἐρήμου μᾶλλον ἢ τῆς ἐχούσης τὸν ἄνδρα: ἐπεὶ ἔρημος ἐδόκει εἶναι ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ὁ λαὸς ἡμῶν. νυνὶ δὲ πιστεύσαντες πλείονες ἐγενόμεθα τῶν δοκούντων ἔχειν θεόν.
καὶ ἑτέρα δὲ γραφὴ λέγει, ὅτι οὐκ ἦλθον καλέσαι δικαίους, ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλούς:
τοῦτο λέγει, ὅτι δεῖ τοὺς ἀπολλυμένους σώζειν.
ἐκεῖνο γάρ ἐστιν μέγα καὶ θαυμαστὸν οὐ τὰ ἑστῶτα στηρίζειν, ἀλλὰ τὰ πίπτοντα.
οὕτως καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς ἠθέλησεν σῶσαι τὰ ἀπολλύμενα, καὶ ἔσωσεν πολλούς, ἐλθὼν καὶ καλέσας ἡμᾶς ἤδη ἀπολλυμένους.
orientation: The preacher is applying Isaiah's words about the barren woman to the church, which was once barren but now has many children through faith.
pass_a_gloss: Rejoice, barren one who does not bear; break forth and shout, you who are not in labor; because many are the children of the desolate one, more than of her who has the husband. What he said: Rejoice, barren one who does not bear, he said about us: for our church was barren before children were given to her. And what he said: Shout, you who are not in labor, this means: that we should offer up our prayers simply to God, not as those in labor should we grow weary. And what he said: Because many are the children of the desolate one, more than of her who has the husband: since our people seemed to be desolate, away from God. But now, having believed, we have become more numerous than those who seem to have God. And another scripture also says, that I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners. This means, that it is necessary to save those who are perishing. For that is great and wonderful, not to support the things that stand, but the things that fall. So also Christ willed to save the things that were perishing, and he saved many, coming and calling us who were already perishing.

choices.why: Keeps the feminine singular force of the Greek adjective used substantivally, matching Isaiah's address to the barren woman.

choices.english: you who are not in labor
choices.why: Preserves the participial construction and the present tense, emphasizing the ongoing state of not being in labor.
rejected: you who have not been in labor

choices.why: Keeps the substantival use of the adjective, matching the parallel with 'her who has the husband' and the later explanation that the people seemed desolate from God.
Preserves the adverb 'simply' and the infinitive of purpose, conveying that prayers should be offered without the weariness of labor pains.
Keeps the neuter plural participle with the imperfect periphrastic force, matching the earlier 'those who are perishing' and emphasizing the ongoing state.
Preserves the hortatory subjunctive with the negative, conveying the exhortation not to grow weary as those in labor do.

pass_b_english: "Rejoice, barren one who bears no children; break forth and shout, you who are not in labor, for the children of the desolate one are more numerous than the children of her who has a husband" (Isaiah 54:1). When he said, "Rejoice, barren one who bears no children," he was speaking about us. For our church was barren before children were given to her.
And when he said, "Shout, you who are not in labor," this is what he means: we should offer up our prayers to God simply, and not grow weary as women in labor do.

And when he said, "For the children of the desolate one are more numerous than the children of her who has a husband," he said this because our people once seemed desolate, abandoned by God. But now that we have believed, we have become more numerous than those who seemed to have God.

And another scripture says, "I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners" (Matthew 9:13). This means that he must save those who are perishing. For the great and wonderful thing is not to support what is standing, but what is falling. So also Christ willed to save the things that were perishing, and he saved many, coming and calling us when we were already perishing.

last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ ἑτέρα δὲ γραφὴ λέγει, ὅτι οὐκ ἦλθον καλέσαι δικαίους, ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλούς
last_rejected.why: Source says 'another scripture says' with first-person 'I came not,' but English attributes to Matthew and changes to third person 'I did not come.' The source quotes Jesus speaking in first person, matching Mark 2:17/Luke 5:32, not Matthew 9:13's third-person report. The citation should note the first-person form or cite Mark/Luke.
last_rejected.fix: another scripture says, 'I came not to call the righteous, but sinners' (Mark 2:17; cf. Luke 5:32)
last_rejected.ruling: Matthew 9:13 reports Jesus' first-person words; citation is standard. Third-person 'I did not come' is English syntax for the quote, not the narrator.
